newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: UN's Annan grants immunity to special investigator.
newsitem.headline: UN's Annan grants immunity to special investigator.

text.p: A Malaysian lawyer working for the United Nations said on Tuesday he had been assured by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan of immunity from prosecution for statements made in the course of duty.

Param Cumaraswamy said he would now apply to a Malaysian court to dismiss a $23 million libel case brought against him in December by lawyer V. Kanalingam in connection with a magazine article published in 1995.

In the article, Param -- the U.N. Special Rapporteur on Judges and the Judiciary -- was quoted as saying he was investigating complaints that businessmen were manipulating the Malaysian judicial system.
Two Malaysian firms, MBf Capital Bhd and MBf Northern Securities Sdn Bhd, have also brought a $24 million libel suit against Param over the article.

Param had argued that his U.N. position as a special investigator allowed him immunity against the suit by the MBf companies. But Malaysia's High Court ruled last month that he did not have such protection and forced him to file for defence.
A senior U.N. official described the court decision as a dangerous precedent for usurping the authority of the U.N. secretary-general.

Kofi Annan's notice, shown to the media by Param and addressed to Malaysian authorities, said that Param had immunity from prosecution for words expressed during the course of his work as a U.N. investigator.
"The Secretary-General has determined that the words which constitute the basis of plaintiff's complaint in this case were spoken by the Special Rapporteur in the course of his mission," it said.
"The Secretary-General, therefore, maintains that...Param Cumaraswamy is immune from legal process with respect thereto."

Param, a prominent Malaysian lawyer and once chairman of the country's bar council, said the core of his defence was that the observations he made in the article were true and had also been expressed by top Malaysian leaders.
"Very simply I have pleaded the truth of the comments I made," he said.

"The same concerns were expressed subsequently and in a similar vein by the prime minister, the deputy prime minister, even the chief justice, and earlier by the judge who heard these matters in court."

In a joint letter last week, U.N. legal experts urged Annan to take further steps to protect Param, saying that immunity from the legal process granted to U.N. specialists under a 1946 convention had been undermined by the Malaysian courts.
The Geneva-based Centre for the Independence of Judges and Lawyers has called on Annan to bring the case of Param's immunity before the International Court of Justice.
